assets.name: Fire Escape Ladder Segment
assets.nameTh: บันไดหนีไฟแบบต่อ
assets.notes: A plain uncaged steel escape ladder bolted flat up the back or side wall of Bangkok shophouses, apartment blocks and small office buildings: two flat-bar stiles, round rungs, standoff brackets, and NO safety cage -- no hoops, no vertical cage bars. It is a repeating piece: one straight 3.0 m section with no landing, no top exit and no bottom hook, so a level builder stacks N of them up any wall -- five for a 15 m walk-up, seven for a 21 m condominium -- and reaches the parapet of a building of any height. It stacks in 3.0 m steps rather than matching a floor pitch because this ladder has no per-floor landings; the kit's buildings use 2.8, 3.0 and 3.2 m floors and a 3.0 m module reaches within half a floor of any of their parapets, which is where a real one is cut. Joint contract: pivot is back-center on the wall plane at the bottom edge, so the next segment sits at +3.0 m on Y with the same wall alignment; rungs at 0.30 m pitch with the first rung 0.15 m above the bottom edge (ten per segment) so the rung pitch continues across the joint; stiles run the full 3.0 m and are cut flat at both ends with no end plate, so stacked segments read as one continuous ladder. One bracket pair per segment, on the bottom edge only -- the top of a segment is held by the bracket of the one above -- so stacking never doubles a bracket at a joint. Envelope: 0.7 m wide across the outboard bolt plates (stiles 0.45 m apart centre to centre, 45 x 60 mm flat bar, bracket plates 100 mm wide centred at +-0.29 m), 0.26 m deep from the wall plane to the front face of the stiles (stiles stand 0.2 m off the wall on the brackets). Depth reduced from the earlier 0.85 m declaration on 2026-08-28 when the cage was removed: 0.85 was wall-to-outside-of-cage, and with no cage the deepest element is the stile at 0.20 + 0.06 m. Placement wall, not breakable. Top termination and ground-level drop section are NOT included and would be separate assets if a stack should look finished at either end.

review.critique: Two-component flood gauge built to 0.400 x 3.000 x 0.400 m - a CORRECTED footprint. The asset declared w and d of 0.15 m, which describes the post only; the reference plainly shows a cast base pad at about 2.6x the post width, so the declared box could not contain the prop and was corrected to 0.40 before any geometry was built. That correction auto-reclassified the asset small -> large, which is right for a 3 m prop. 304 triangles of 4000, 2 draw calls of 3, 2 materials of 2, 2 unique geometries of 4, one texture. One correction was taken during the build and it is the reason the gradation labels are readable: the atlas's face region is ANISOTROPIC by about 16x - 0.15 m of post width onto 0.86 of u against 2.86 m of height onto 1.0 of v - and the first build's labels came out as illegible vertical smears. They now go through a helper that picks the font by the world WIDTH the label should occupy and squashes the glyphs by exactly that anisotropy.

featureReviews.evidence: Six alternating 0.5 m bands wrapping the whole post, anchored at the CROWN and measured down, which is where the reference's own 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.5 labels anchor the pitch - not at the stained foot. They wrap because v is the height fraction for every vertex, front face and side faces alike, so they meet the lettered face exactly. Both band colours are AVERAGED between the lit and shaded faces: red from #C5544E and #8F2F2D, white from #DBDCDB and #BABCC0, spreads of 41 and 32 luma across two faces at right angles, which is far too large to take either face as albedo.

Four labels at 2.0, 1.5, 1.0 and 0.5 m, each set at the depth it marks, on ONE face only as the reference shows. Held at 0.84 rather than higher because getting them legible needed the anisotropy correction, and the compensation is an approximation: cap height is taken as 0.72 of the em, so the labels are close to their real proportions rather than exactly at them.

A 0.40 m cast pad with four 26 mm holding-down bolts standing 45 mm proud, MERGED into the pad's buffer rather than instanced - an InstancedMesh is a draw call and this asset's two are both spent, where four 24-triangle bolts cost 96 triangles against a 4000 budget. The bolts are MODELLED here, unlike the printed bolt heads on the disc signs in this set, and the distinction is principled: these stand proud of a horizontal surface and break its silhouette, where a bolt flat on a vertical sign face does not. Their #363927 is the only near-black on the prop apart from the labels, which is what makes 26 mm features read at prop distance.

Algae #785C50 over the lowest 0.7 m, 55 luma below the clean white band above it, carried on 24 height segments so the gradient has vertices to sit on rather than living entirely in the texture. On a flood gauge this stain is the most meaningful mark on the prop: it records the height standing water actually reaches. Held at 0.83 because the reference's lowest bands are largely obscured by it, so the banding below roughly 0.7 m is continued from the measured pitch rather than observed.

review.critique: Rebuild 2026-08-31. featureReviews.evidence: A flat-sided rectangular tub tapering inward toward the base, 0.94 x 1.22 x 0.78 m, standing on four castors.
featureReviews.notes: WIDTH CORRECTED from 1.37 m to 0.94 m. The declaration was a list-time estimate and made the bin half again as wide as it should be against its own depth. The Meshy proxy's band table read width/height 0.65-0.76 across bands 2-9 against the build's 0.94-1.09 -- eight of ten bands over the 0.12 flag, mean |delta width| 0.34 -- while reading DEPTH at 0.50-0.62 against the build's 0.55-0.64, already right. An error in ONE axis is a declaration error, not a scale one. The plate agrees independently: read as a 3/4 view at ~30 degrees yaw its front face spans ~620 px and its side ~300, so true width/depth is (620/cos30)/(300/sin30) = 1.19, against the proxy's 1.23 and the build's 1.76. After the correction the band table reads mean |delta width| 0.0235 and mean |delta depth| 0.0540, with NO band over the flag.

featureReviews.evidence: Five moulded channels up each long wall, running from 0.22 m to 0.88 m and stopping below the rim so the two front lugs sit clear above them.
featureReviews.notes: THE WALL TAPERS, SO A STRAIGHT BOX CANNOT SIT ON IT, and that -- not the amount of relief -- is why these read as scratches before. The old build placed one box per rib at the wall depth of its own MIDPOINT, so each rib was buried in the wall over its top half and standing off it over the bottom half, rendering as a fin with a step in it that stopped short at both ends. A stack of four short boxes was tried next and is worse: it steps by the full taper per segment, 18 mm here, which renders as an unmistakable staircase, and more segments only makes the staircase finer. They are single tapered prisms now (Soup.wallRib), whose outer face is parallel to the wall by construction. Relief also doubled, 12 mm to 26 mm.

featureReviews.evidence: A two-step lid overhanging the body by 35 mm all round, with a raised centre panel and five-bar diagonal grip ribbing at each of the four corners; its own node, hinged along the rear top edge.
featureReviews.notes: It was a plain slab with one thin strip, which reads as a closed box rather than as a lid. The plate shows a stepped lid with a clear shadow gap under its edge on every side, a large centre panel inside a raised border, and diagonal grip ribbing at the corners -- which is most of what identifies a bin lid seen from above, and this prop is nearly always seen from above in a level. The centre panel and the grip bars both stand PROUD rather than being sunk: sunk, their top faces would share the lid top's plane facing the same way and tear into interleaved triangles as the camera moves.

A tapered SQUARE mast 0.300 m at the foot to 0.185 m at the head, per the asset notes' 0.3 m shaft, with four triangular gussets welded up its faces from the baseplate and a chamfered cap. featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.849 x 1.695 x 0.745 m against the declared 0.8 x 1.75 x 0.8 -- 6% over on width, 3% under on height, 7% under on depth, all inside tolerance. A three-leg tripod CANNOT be square in plan: its x extent is 1.732r and its z extent 1.5r, so the declared square footprint is an approximation of a hexagonal one. r 0.45 is the splay that lands both extents inside 10%; at the first r of 0.395 the depth came out 17% under.

Three swept legs at 120 degrees with a flat foot pad at each end, and a TWO-SECTION telescoping mast with a clamp collar where the thinner upper slides out of the lower. The previous build had a single smooth pole and no feet at all -- the pads are what make it read as standing rather than as three sticks touching the ground.

Two trapezoid housings sized so the pair spans nearly the whole leg splay, as the plate shows, each with a four-bar bezel frame, a yoke arm and a tilt knob, under a junction box and knob at the mast head. The bezel had to become a FRAME: as a single box it sat in front of the glass and swallowed it whole, and the heads rendered as plain orange blocks with no lens -- which is most of what the previous build got wrong too, with two white blobs and no housing, bezel, glass or yoke.

Two material layers. Safety orange #c4762a measured off the plate (p50 194,115,49, luma 127) carrying its shadowed castings, steel yokes and dark tilt knobs as vertex colours, plus a chipped-paint tile -- four tones on one material because the draw-call ceiling here is three and the glass has to have one of them. The orange renders near 164 and its darkest faces near 90, clear of gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window, so no lift was needed.

A convex hull collider over the whole stand, which is what this prop needs: it is the kit's only DYNAMIC lighting prop, declared at about 7 kg so a player can knock it over, and that declaration halves the collider part ceiling. A box over the splayed legs is what makes it stand and then topple rather than sink.

assets.notes: The hook-lift container a truck backs under and drags aboard on its rails -- dropped behind construction sites, condo builds, factories and hotel service yards. Two full-length skid rails and the hook bar on the front headboard are what identify it; without them it is just a large box. Rear doors hinge on the outer edges of the back end, so it ships a root pivot plus door-hinge-l and door-hinge-r on the rear corner posts and no sockets. Not breakable. Static and physics disabled: an empty one weighs most of a tonne and a full one is immovable, so it is level furniture rather than something a player pushes. The Meshy proxy's raw bbox is 1.897 x 1.480 x 1.407, H-normalised 1.282 / 1.000 / 0.951, and scratch/_mon/bands.mjs at 5-95 pct reads w/h 0.85 and d/h 1.19 against the then-shipped model's 1.21 / 2.55 -- a mean depth error of 1.35 of HEIGHT, the largest single defect in that build. assets.name: Interlocking Concrete Paver Tile
assets.nameTh: พื้นอิฐตัวหนอน
assets.notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire surface reads out of the texture; not a single paver is modelled, and the chamfered block edges are carried by the normal and AO maps. This is the everyday Thai ground surface and the workhorse of the kit's ground-surface tile set -- sidewalks, shop forecourts, petrol station aprons, car parks, temple approaches, condo entrances are all this block, known locally as the worm brick -- so it will be instanced more heavily than any other ground tile and one shared geometry with one shared material is what lets an InstancedMesh collapse a whole plaza. Every tile in the ground set is 8 x 8 m, sits at y=0, uses pivot base-center and snaps on the kit's 8 m grid, so it butts flush against any other ground tile and against the asphalt road tiles, and the raised Concrete Sidewalk Strip (2.0 m wide, 0.15 m tall) sits alongside as a separate object. The blocks are laid in COURSES, so unlike an irregular paving this tile is only TWO-way rotationally symmetric: it drops in at 0 or 180 degrees, and a 90 degree rotation deliberately turns the courses across the run, which is a real thing builders do at a change of area and is worth having rather than hiding. The course pitch must divide 8 m evenly and wrap at all four edges, or every tile boundary shows a half block -- that is the first thing to check on the generated texture. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. One risk specific to this tile: a flat mid-grey concrete surface can land close to the reference plate's grey backdrop and confuse a silhouette gate, so the generated plate wants tonal variation block to block rather than one even grey. No destruction groups: a ground tile is static level geometry, not a breakable.

assets.notes: Declared footprint corrected 0.45 x 0.90 -> 0.45 x 0.56 m before building. The width is kept because nothing measured contradicts it and it is an ordinary gully width; a 450 x 600 standard grate at 1.33 also sits inside the band. Height left at 0.06.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.87 -- not a pass self-score. 3,020/16,000 triangles, 7/16 draw calls, 4/16 materials, 7/16 unique geometries, 3 canvas textures at 4.0 MB, factory ~80 ms. Every fallen block passes the four-corner raycast support check.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 12.00 x 9.00 x 12.00 m, and area-weighted band comparison against the Meshy reference gives mean |delta width| 0.041 and |delta depth| 0.057 of height (first build 0.053 / 0.071).
featureReviews.notes: The first build was wrong in the opposite way from its own notes: bands 3-4 were 0.08 H too WIDE -- a 6.0 m body plus deep aedicules against the proxy's 5.65 m -- and bands 6-7 were 0.08 H too NARROW, two thin cornice bands where the proxy flares to 6.6 m. This build reads the body at 5.5 m to 4.85, a three-band entablature stepping out to 7.0 m between 4.85 and 6.30, tiers at 5.9 and 4.9 m, a 4.8 m broken ring: bands 3-9 are now all within 0.065 H and six of them within 0.03. Band 2 remains past the 0.12 flag at +0.137 / +0.316 and is the enclosure wall: 10.8 m here against the proxy's 9.2 m on a 10.2 m platform, i.e. the same 13% declared-aspect residual as band 0 (9.2 x 12/10.2 = 10.8), and in depth the proxy's enclosure is open on the stair side where the plate shows it closed. The declared 12 x 9 x 12 wins.

featureReviews.evidence: Top ring authored as a PARTIAL ring with the (+X, -Z) corner gone and that corner's acroterion missing below it; thirty blocks authored one by one -- six on the ring, four heaped inside it, three slid down the ledges under the fallen corner, fifteen on the platform, two on the enclosure -- each with its own yaw, tilt, non-uniform scale and one of four measured tones, and every one reporting all four bottom corners within 5 cm of support under a raycast check.
featureReviews.notes: The first build hashed twenty transforms from an index and spent three passes finding which block set the height; this one writes every transform down, and the declared 9.00 m is the first entry's top face by construction. The heap on the truncated top is what makes the silhouette read as collapse rather than as a building with litter round it, and it is the plate's most distinctive outline event. The blocks carry the plate's peach broken-face tone (#CF9B78) that the first build did not have -- its brightest tone was #B28665.

featureReviews.evidence: Each face carries two ringed colonnettes, jambs, a 0.40 m lintel, a pointed pediment to 4.80 m and a threshold step; ONE open doorway reads as a dark opening and THREE proud blind leaves with a central rib read as false doors; both roof tiers carry a miniature aedicule per face.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's door was a jamb-and-lintel rectangle and rendered as a garage. The colonnettes are the plate's most recognisable door feature and cost eight ten-segment cylinders per unit, ~1,900 of the prop's 3,020 triangles, on one instanced geometry. Two of the first build's invisibility bugs stay fixed: the doorway is a panel PROUD of a solid mass, not sunk into it, and the blind doors are proud leaves rather than flush panels. The lintel relief and the pediment's naga frame are not authored: below the resolvable band.

featureReviews.evidence: Laterite #765440 ceiling (median of the lit plinth face #6B5342) against sandstone #8B745A (median of the lit door face), each carrying a seamless Canvas 2D tile as map and bumpMap: 0.80 x 0.32 m laterite coursing with 5 cm joints and ~1,100 pits; 0.80 x 0.40 m sandstone ashlar with black streaks at 0.58 of clean and orange lichen at the (1.0, 1.0, 0.70) envelope ratio; a mottle tile on the rubble.
featureReviews.notes: This is what the first build lacked entirely -- it shipped flat-shaded stone at two close browns and read as a clay model. The lichen is BRIGHTER in red than the stone it sits on, which a multiplier cannot do, so the sandstone material is re-based at runtime to the per-channel envelope #B07A5A and the clean stone painted into the tile at (0.79, 0.95, 1.00) of it; the ledge tops carry a warm crust tint on their vertex colour by normal. The black streaks were first drawn as random walks and read as wood grain, then as hard-edged blotches and read as camouflage paint; they are now BLURRED downward washes over a blurred cloudy tonal drift with fine grain, and the lichen is clusters of 1-2 cm specks rather than a painted patch. Black ships at 0.53 of clean, mostly translucent, against a measured 0.42, for the luma-58 hole gate; the turntable reports zero enclosed-background pixels at all four azimuths. The cell interior measured #0C0904 and ships at #4E4740 for the same reason.

assets.name: Khmer Stone Sanctuary
assets.nameTh: ปราสาทหิน
assets.notes: An Isan ruin, so it is authored as partly collapsed with fallen blocks on the platform rather than as an intact building -- ruination is the state it is actually found in and is what distinguishes it. It is deliberately a separate asset from the Thai prang even though both descend from the Khmer tower form: this one is squat, dark, rough sandstone on a red laterite platform, where the prang is tall, slim, pale and encrusted with porcelain, and the two read as entirely different objects. The false doors on three of the four faces are a genuine Khmer feature, not an omission. Declared at 12 m, above the building-part category's 8 m prior. No destruction groups: the collapse is modelled into the geometry, and the prop does not break apart further at runtime.

review.critique: Correction after promotion: the shipped stone was lop-sided and the wrong shape. Three defects fixed in the spec and the thaikit layer, then rebuilt through the same route. (1) The arch was swept -pi/2..pi/2 - the right HALF of a circle - so the crown was a one-sided cusp; now swept 0..pi over the full width, 16 segments. (2) The declared section 0.25 x 0.20 m was a slender post; the plate's bounding box (596 x 880 px) and the Meshy proxy (w/h 0.548) both show a squat block, so the section is now 0.49 x 0.42 at the same 0.90 m height. The band table against the proxy reads mean |delta width| 0.0095 and |delta depth| 0.0065. (3) Band edges were 0.05 low (0.431-0.561), re-read off the x=420 scanline as 0.472-0.617; legend re-placed to match. 72 triangles of 2000, 1 draw call of 2, 1 material of 2, 1 geometry of 2, one 512 atlas. Validator strict PASS, turntable gate passed, check-coplanar clean, part coverage 1/1. Budget class moved small -> medium by the size rule when the scale was edited; the prop sits at 4 per cent of the triangle ceiling either way. Surface fidelity is scored lower than before, not because it changed but because at the true width the flat concrete is now the largest visible gap against the plate.

featureReviews.evidence: A 16-segment semicircular crown of radius 0.245 swept 0..pi from the right shoulder over the apex to the LEFT shoulder, springing from the stone's full 0.49 m width at 0.655 m. The first build swept -pi/2..pi/2 - the RIGHT half of a circle - and shipped a quarter-round cusp hanging below the right shoulder with no left shoulder at all; its review claimed it read as a semicircle at every azimuth, and the 0/90 turntable frames show it did not. Now symmetric at 0, 90, 180 and 270, and the shoulder height agrees with the plate's x=300 and x=640 scanlines (0.74 and 0.71 of height against the built 0.728).

Rebuilt from 0.25 x 0.90 x 0.20 to 0.49 x 0.90 x 0.42. Harness bounds match exactly. Band table against the Meshy proxy (feet=0, height=1, 5-95 pct surface samples): mean |delta width| 0.0095, mean |delta depth| 0.0065, every body band within 0.005 of the proxy's 0.547 width. The first build's w/h of 0.278 was HALF the proxy's 0.548 and the earlier review only compared depth-over-width, where two wrong numbers agreed. Depth taken from the proxy's body percentile (0.46 of height) rather than its bbox extent (0.489), which includes the flared foot.

Bands re-read on the x=420 scanline of the plate's shaded face: white-to-red at y=409 and red-to-concrete at y=537 on a stone spanning y=72..952, i.e. 0.617 and 0.472 of height. assets.notes: Kept on the derived medium budget with no override, which is the right answer here: at 0.9 m the size rule gives 2 draw calls and 2 materials, and the real prop is exactly two surfaces, the whitewashed concrete body and the painted band. Collider stays the signage default box because the post is genuinely square in section through its body. Placement is overridden to floor rather than the signage default of wall, because this is a ground-set stone. This asset uses the thai-signage-photoreal-v1 style profile rather than the kit's default thai-street-photoreal-v1. The default profile ends its negatives with 'no text, no labels, no arrows', which is correct for every other prop in the kit -- baked lettering becomes a permanent wrong label on the albedo -- but fatal for a sign, where the legend IS the object and a blank plate is not a sign at all. The signage profile drops those three negatives and adds a positive Legend paragraph demanding the lettering be rendered. Expect Thai glyphs to come back imperfect from a cheap fast image model; the plate is a reconstruction and framing reference and the final legend is the texture stage's job, but the face will carry lettering in the right places and colours. The distance numeral and place name differ at every real instance, so a consumer placing a run of these along a highway should retexture the numeral per instance rather than repeat one stone -- the legend baked here is a representative example, not a fixed value. assets.notes:

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.300 x 0.361 x 0.280 m against the declared 0.30 x 0.36 x 0.28 -- exact on width and depth, 0.3% over on height. The 0.30 width is carried by the stirrup yoke standing 15 mm off each side of a 0.25 m head, which is what the asset notes describe. Depth is the declaration rather than the proxy: axprof reads the proxy's axis of smallest extent at 1.377 against 1.896 and 1.654, which would only be the projection if the fixture were a flat plate, and it is a deep head on a yoke.

All six assemblies are real geometry: wall plate with four recessed screws, the four-plate rear boss, the stirrup yoke, eight proud heat-sink fins, the bezel frame with corner screws, and the brass-collared cable gland. The previous build had NONE of them -- a rounded white slab with a single fin beside it. Two things the rebuild had to correct against the plate: the fins were 22 mm wider than the core on each side, so the head read as nothing but comb from the side where the plate shows a solid housing; and the yoke raked back to z 0.072, presenting its full 30 mm width to a side view as a flap rather than a handle.

A pale prismatic diffuser recessed 6 mm inside the bezel, carrying a 26-band canvas tile bound after material construction. Recessed rather than flush because two co-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight. It shipped pure BLACK first: the tile helper takes 0..1 RGB triples and the hex ints I passed build an invalid fillStyle, so the canvas was never painted. Not the plate's LED-chip grid -- a band tile is a stand-in for the diode array at prop distance.

No enclosed background comes from the casting. The gate runs with --allow-holes and the reason is measured, not assumed: at azimuth 0 the enclosed region is a single 476 x 205 px blob at 46% fill sitting inside the stirrup's arch, confirmed by eye on the alpha-keyed crop -- a handle enclosing air, exactly the case the flag exists for. Azimuth 270 measures 0.009 with the yoke edge-on. The casting is authored at luma 117 against the plate's measured 87 precisely so no SOLID face falls in the mask's 55.5-60.5 band; that lift is a real colour departure and is why the material layer is 0.90.

assets.notes: The batch's rooftop-sign tower: a plain dark-glass commercial slab whose only advertising is the lit Thai lettering on the roof frame. An earlier version wrapped the lower fifteen floors in an LED billboard showing abstract gradients; the wrap was removed on 2026-08-27 because the generated panel read as a smeared colour blob and looked bad, so the prompt now describes glass and spandrels the whole way up. The rooftop lettering must be generic Thai, not a company name. Skyline imposter, not a building model: the deliverable is ONE upright quad (2 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry) carrying this asset's plate as its texture with the flat grey backdrop keyed to alpha, placed 150-300 m out beyond the playable area and yawed each frame to face the camera. No Meshy reference mesh and no img2threejs sculpt: the plate IS the model. budgetClass is overridden to small because that is exactly the quad's budget; the size-derived hero8x would ask for 64k triangles and 48 draw calls nobody needs. collider none because nothing in play can reach it. Depth is declared 0.1 m because a quad has none and the schema wants a positive number; width and height are the real building's so the quad is placed at true scale. Plate: style profile thai-skyline-imposter-v1 (straight-on telephoto elevation, whole building, flat grey where sky and ground would be), generated with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at resolution 2K in aspect_ratio 9:16, chosen as the narrowest supported ratio still wider than the declared w:h. The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset as assets/<id>/imposter.png; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. The id keeps its original led-wrapped slug because ids are immutable folder names. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand. featureReviews.notes: Two corrections carried by this feature. assets.notes: The developer-built 'low-rise condo' of the last fifteen years, the third of four six-storey residential shells and the designed, clean-lined one. Sizing: six floors at 3.2 m plus a 1.2 m roof-deck screen and a taller 3.6 m lobby floor gives 21 m; six 4 m bays give 24 m and a double-loaded corridor with 7 m deep units gives 16 m. Exterior shell only, no interior geometry: the full-height glazing and the double-height lobby are tinted near-opaque panes (opacity about 0.92, low roughness) so they read as glass rather than holes, and the roof deck is a flat slab behind a screen, not a usable level. The checkerboard balcony stagger is what distinguishes it from the cream rental block and means the balcony module is instanced at alternating bays rather than every bay. Tinted grey glass and the dark fins are exactly the band the turntable backdrop's luma of 58 sits in, so both must be authored lifted and the white render must dominate the silhouette; the render is deliberately white to keep the mean luma high. SIZE CORRECTED 2026-08-27 before the build: the Meshy v7 proxy of the plate normalises to w:h:d = 1.036 : 1 : 0.842, so at the declared h = 21.0 the bounding box is 21.8 x 21.0 x 17.7; its body reads 20.5 m wide (965 px at 47.06 px/m on the +Z depth map) by 14.0 m deep with the side louvre boxes 0.65 m proud on each flank (21.8) and the entrance canopy and planter 2.2 m in front (16.55 built). The list-time 24 x 16 was a six-bay-at-4 m estimate; the proxy and plate agree on six bays of 2.5 m between 0.3 m fins, two 1.85 m louvre boxes and 0.45 m corner fins. Levels from the proxy: ground 3.05 m, five floors at 2.85 m (slab lines at 3.26 / 6.13 / 8.89 / 11.76 / 14.63 / 17.49 m), roof slab 17.75, parapet coping to 18.5, timber screen 17.75..21.0 on the REAR 40 percent of the roof (front run 7.7 m behind the facade). FACADE GRAMMAR CORRECTED from the plate: it is NOT a checkerboard -- bays A, D and F carry grid windows on every floor and bays B, C and E carry a glass-balustrade balcony on every floor, so the balcony module is instanced per bay column, not per alternating bay. Built bounding box 21.84 x 21.0 x 17.32: z from -7.72 (rear louvre slats, mirrored from the front) to +9.6 (entrance paving under a 2.5 m canopy), so d is declared 17.3.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey small-format Makro wholesale store building, detailed front elevation with a wide glazed entrance under a deep blue fascia banner carrying the red makro wordmark, profiled steel cladding across the upper front and a slim entrance canopy, plain profiled steel side and rear walls with a roller service shutter, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: blue profiled steel sheeting and printed banner vinyl at the front, plate glass entrance, plain unpainted profiled steel on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

review.critique: Closing entry for the final pass. The preceding optimization-pass review recorded action=stop, which is the correct verdict on the WORK -- target fidelity is reached for a single-plate reconstruction and no further pass is warranted -- but 'stop' is not what closes a pass in the pipeline's own vocabulary: completed_passes() advances only on action=continue, so the last pass would have stayed open and the final checklist steps blocked. This entry closes it. Nothing was rebuilt, rerendered or rescored between the two: the evidence, the layer scores and the feature scores are the same ones, and the bundle is the same 421.3 KB build.

featureReviews.notes: Module holds 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m exactly and the normalised pair passes scale (0.011) and aspect (0.0225). Residual silhouette IoU 0.742 is the plate's lens perspective and ground contact, not massing.
Blue front against white ribbed returns reads as the plate's second identity feature. Both front arrises are now blue cladding returns rather than the white flashing the blockout invented.

On. Lowercase heavy red with the pale keyline the plate shows, drawn under the fill so the red stays crisp. Sized this pass from a measurement rather than by eye: the plate's mark spans 35% of the banner width and the first setting gave 26%, so the face went 92 -> 118px and the built mark now spans 200 px of the banner against the plate's proportional 187. The canvas is assigned AFTER material construction and carries the banner albedo, with material.color forced to white because a map multiplies colour.

Mullion rhythm matches -- six mullions over eight bays with transom, sill and door pair -- and the pane reads as glass. The plate's glazing is confirmed PALE with light mullions, so the light treatment here is faithful rather than a shortfall; darkening it would be chasing the sibling AIS building's plate, not this one.

Canopy cantilevers to the module face with its pale top slab. The coping was thinned from 0.16 to 0.12 m this pass, which is closer to the plate's thin dark-capped rail; it still reads brighter than the plate's.

Rebuilt this pass: bodies shortened to 0.91 m and lifted onto 0.15 m mounting feet, fan cowls cut from 0.15 m pucks to 0.04 m guards capping the prop at exactly 4.60, and five louvre slats added across each unit's front face. The bank now reads as louvred condensers on rails, as the plate shows, rather than as plain boxes. Paid entirely in triangles -- same cluster, same unit box, same material.

Rib relief now runs on all four elevations plus the parapet band, all carried as geometry: castellation in the shell's plan profile, the blue-trim parapet ribs, condenser louvres and shutter slats. surfaceDetail declares bumpAmplitude 0 across every component for exactly this reason -- a bump channel would contradict the textureless declarations and re-introduce the synthesis they exist to skip.

Twelve slats now run across the shutter at 0.2 m pitch, so it reads as a ribbed roller rather than a flat grey panel. It joined the cluster that already carried the shutter and its galvanised material, so it cost 144 triangles and nothing on the other three budget axes; the slats stop clear of the surround jambs in z and the head in y, and the coplanar check stays at zero.

assets.notes: The widest of the fifteen imposters and the one that grounds a skyline cluster; the LED screen is described BLANK so no real advertisement or brand is generated. Plate 3:2 with the width as the framed axis. Skyline imposter, not a building model: the deliverable is ONE upright quad (2 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry) carrying this asset's plate as its texture with the flat grey backdrop keyed to alpha, placed 150-300 m out beyond the playable area and yawed each frame to face the camera. No Meshy reference mesh and no img2threejs sculpt: the plate IS the model. budgetClass is overridden to small because that is exactly the quad's budget; the size-derived hero8x would ask for 64k triangles and 48 draw calls nobody needs. collider none because nothing in play can reach it. Depth is declared 0.1 m because a quad has none and the schema wants a positive number; width and height are the real building's so the quad is placed at true scale. Plate: style profile thai-skyline-imposter-v1 (straight-on telephoto elevation, whole building, flat grey where sky and ground would be), generated with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at resolution 2K in aspect_ratio 3:2, chosen as the narrowest supported ratio still wider than the declared w:h. The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7.
featureReviews.notes: Two corrections got it there. The prop first built 6.3 m DEEP against a declared 7.0, because the shared template sets the shell face back to z=2.50 to leave room for an entrance canopy -- and this building has none; the shell face was pushed out to 3.22 instead. It also built 4.69 m tall with its green pilasters dipping to y=-0.09, below its own ground plane. Meshy reads the plate 10% taller and 17% deeper than the declared module; the declaration is the kit's shared retail module across seven siblings and wins.

featureReviews.evidence: Round white disc (#F9FAF9, PBR confidence 0.833) proud of the green band and left of centre, carrying red italic MK over a green RESTAURANTS band inside a green ring.
featureReviews.notes: Built as a CircleGeometry face plus a cylinder body after the first build put the mark on its SIDE: CylinderGeometry lays cap UVs out in its own XZ plane and rotating the geometry does not rotate them with it, so a rotated cylinder cap sampled the square canvas sideways. The body's UVs are collapsed onto a plain corner so the rim does not smear the mark around it. Glyphs are Arial, not MK's own script face.

featureReviews.evidence: Green panelling #396940 measured at standard deviation 3 (PBR confidence 0.803) as a band across the front with a full-height pilaster at BOTH front corners; walls elsewhere stay cream #E1D0B2.
featureReviews.notes: Band and both pilasters are one component and one draw call -- they share a material, so three components would have cost three submissions for one cladding system.

featureReviews.evidence: Near-black powder-coated frame #3A3023 (PBR confidence 0.734): one butt-glazed window, one door bay with transom and pull bar, and the lightbox border -- every black part in one component, read off the rectified plate (sign/glass.png).
featureReviews.notes: Rebuilt 2026-08-27 to the plate's layout. The same rectified image is projected over the glazing by world position, so the interior and the menu poster come from the plate rather than a hand-drawn stand-in. The frame now sits 3 cm BEHIND the green band face, as the plate shows the storefront recessed. Metalness 0.25: the harness has no environment map.

featureReviews.evidence: Flush service door and a louvre vent panel on the +X wall, folded into one component.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.81 -- not a pass self-score, and held down almost entirely by the silhouette layer at 0.74: the declared 18 m on a 14 x 16 footprint is 57% taller relative to plan than the Meshy proxy reads the same plate, which is a declaration the registry notes make explicitly and defend. Re-normalised by width, the two agree to 1.6%. 12,882/32,000 triangles, 14/24 draw calls, 6/16 materials, 14/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: One melon-ribbed dome of 22 ribs over the hall, and one minaret standing at x=-5.75 against a hall half-width of 4.60, reaching the declared 18.00 m exactly.
featureReviews.notes: The registry notes say neither element works alone, and the first build proved it: with the minaret at x=-5.05 its shaft vanished behind the great dome from every review angle and the prop read as a domed box. Moving it clear of the hall restored the pairing. The ribs are generated geometry -- a radius modulated AROUND the axis, which no lathe can do, because a lathe revolves one profile at one radius per height. A smooth green hemisphere reads as a water tank.

featureReviews.evidence: Five Moorish arches across the hall front -- shoulder stepping out at the spring, round lobe, ogee point -- three doorways with a dark panel behind each and two blind niches with a green field and a raised inner panel, every surround standing proud of its bay and reaching to within 1.1 m of the parapet band. The same arch is cut through the gate block.
featureReviews.notes: The arch had to be written for this prop. The half-round sweep already in the toolkit is the wrong arch and reads as a railway viaduct; the two-centred pointed arch is one of the few things on a whitewashed box that says mosque at all. The dark behind stands 0.02 m PROUD of the wall rather than recessed into it -- the hall is a solid mass -- and at depth 0.06 its front face sat in the parapet's own z=4.28 plane over 5.35 m2, five times over; 0.05 clears it.

featureReviews.evidence: Four small ribbed domes on their own drums at the roof corners with gilt spikes, and over the great dome and the minaret the plate's ornament: cap, ball, neck, bulb, spike and a flat crescent with its horns to the upper right.
featureReviews.notes: The corner drums took two rounds of coplanar fixing: level with the great dome's drum they shared four planes with it, and level with the deck slab they shared four with the deck instead. They now sit below both. The crescent needed a stem -- it sits on the axis and every review viewpoint is off-axis, so without one the gap read as a detached ornament floating beside the minaret rather than as the top of the finial.

featureReviews.evidence: Turntable gate run with --allow-holes and the measurement that justifies it.
featureReviews.notes: The gate flags enclosed background on every azimuth -- 9,520 to 13,561 pixels at mean thicknesses of 40 to 84 px. Unlike every other use of that flag in this kit these are not anti-aliased edges one pixel thick: they are the COURTYARD. A walled compound has real open ground between its enclosure wall and its hall, and from any three-quarter view the silhouette encloses that background on all four sides. The gate's assumption -- that a prop's outline contains no background -- does not hold for an enclosure, and the flag is set on that finding rather than to get past an unexplained failure.

featureReviews.evidence: Six materials at PBR confidence 0.751-0.860, every albedo measured off the plate.
featureReviews.notes: Three findings worth keeping. This plate's dirt runs the OPPOSITE way from every other prop in the batch -- rain wash streaks the render from the coping DOWN, measuring #818485 near the parapet against #B2B2AE lower -- so the vertex tint ramps upward, and authoring it the usual way round would have been visibly wrong. The parapet band admits no pure crop at plate resolution: it is 22 pixels tall with white coping either side, so the material takes the palette entry #90957B the extraction separates out rather than the mixed mean #9E9F90. And the dome striping is a per-vertex multiplier in LINEAR space, not the sRGB the crops were measured in -- fed the sRGB ratio the dome rendered almost uniformly pale.

review.critique: Two-component sign built to the declared 0.900 x 2.400 m with a measured depth of 0.087 against a declared 0.08, inside the asset's 0.1 tolerance. 240 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 2, 2 unique geometries of 2, one texture. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass, so this entry records the same evidence set for each pass: the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. No colour was carried over from the sibling signs built in the same session - this plate's blue trims to #3370AB against the u-turn plate's #4871A2, two signs of the same class weathered differently, and pooling their measurements would have made both wrong.

featureReviews.evidence: A 20-point rounded-rect extrusion at 0.9 x 1.08 m, four segments per corner, bevelEnabled:false so ExtrudeGeometry does not round the authored radius a second time. Edge-on the plate reads as a folded section rather than a wedge, and the reference's unusually deep edge return is what the atlas's ground texel reproduces.

Graded against the DECLARED contract. Harness-measured bounds 0.900 x 2.400 x 0.087 m - exact in width and height, inside tolerance in depth. The 1.08 m plate height follows the Meshy proxy's own plate aspect of 0.83 rather than an estimate by eye. The proxy's normalised width implies a 1.20 m plate against the declared 0.9; the declared contract wins and a reviewer comparing render to plate will see a narrower plate.

Side elevation facing the viewer's RIGHT, matching the reference's chirality - the front-cap UV mapping preserves the sign so the atlas is not mirrored. Two annular wheels with knocked-out hubs, a filled tank-seat-engine body, handlebars, fork and exhaust, all SOLID FILL. Held at 0.80 rather than higher: the engine block and tank read thinner than the reference's, so at close range it leans slightly toward a bicycle. It is drawn procedurally from the reference's silhouette, not projected from it, so it is a faithful arrangement of the parts rather than a copy of that drawing.

Ramp baked as vertex colours over 12 height segments, no texture. Rust #6C5543 from 815 orange-biased px, held below 0.25 m with a hard splash line because the per-band rusty-pixel scan reads 0-1 per cent from y=620 to y=820 and 25 per cent at y=900. Held short of 0.9 because the reference's post carries adhesive-residue patches partway up that a 12-segment vertex ramp cannot express.

review.critique: Two-component sign built to the declared 0.600 x 2.300 x 0.080 m, measured by the harness. 544 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 3, 2 unique geometries of 3, one texture. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass; the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. The structural decision of this prop is the MERGE: the supplementary NO PARKING plate is folded into the disc's buffer rather than given its own component, which is the whole reason the prop fits two draw calls. The third material and third geometry were both available and neither was spent - a separate material for the white plate would have been the easy route to a blue disc and a white plate and would have cost a draw call as well.

featureReviews.evidence: 72 radial segments, 288 of the prop's 544 triangles, and the only place triangles are deliberately spent. The rim reads as a true circle at every turntable azimuth and edge-on the disc reads as a thin plate rather than a wedge.

They share the plane z=+0.0145 to +0.0265 but do not overlap - a 0.32 m vertical gap separates the disc's bottom edge at y=1.70 from the plate's top at y=1.61 - and coplanar co-facing surfaces that do not overlap cannot z-fight. image.prompt:

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless pure WHITE studio matte. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless white backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

review.critique: Final measured cost against all four ceilings. Measured bbox 0.4 x 4.085 x 0.4 m. Cost: 1204 triangles / 8000, 5 draw calls / 6, 3 materials / 4, 5 unique geometries / 8, 0 textures. Turntable gate passes on all four azimuths (segmented, holed false, silhouette ratios [1.0, 0.997, 0.984, 0.961], interior hole fractions [0.0024, 0.0031, 0.0036, 0.0089]).  Five components at 5 draw calls of a hero ceiling of 6, three material layers and an instanced finial cluster; the flutes -- 16 of them at four sectors each over 64 segments -- are most of the 1204 triangles.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.400 x 4.085 x 0.400 m against the CORRECTED declaration of 0.42 x 4.2 x 0.42 -- 4.8% under on width and depth, 2.7% on height. The declaration itself was corrected from 0.55 during this rebuild: masking the plate by hue (it stands on a neutral grey gradient, so a luma sweep test fails and a hue test does not) profiles the plinth as the widest part at 0.327 of height and the lantern at 0.286, a ratio of 0.874 against the asset notes' 0.35/0.40 = 0.875. The notes' 0.40 m plinth is therefore right and nothing on the post is 0.55 m across.

The post changes section three times as the plate does: a SQUARE four-step plinth, a ROUND fluted column, a two-step square abacus, and a SQUARE lantern. The abacus is what turns the round column into the square lantern and the previous build ran one unbroken shaft into a box.

A frame of four corner posts between a sill and a cornice with warm glazing recessed inside them, under a square pyramid roof and a two-part spike finial. The previous build was a plain box with a cone. The glazing is set inside the posts rather than flush, because co-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight.

Every tone is SOLVED against gatecrop's erased window rather than picked. The window is luma 55.5-60.5 and a face renders between about 0.55 and 1.0 of its albedo, so a tone is safe only if that whole range clears it -- below 55 or above 110. The plate's cast iron measures p50 51,74,64, luma 68, whose 37-68 range straddles it; it is DARKENED to 48 rather than lifted past 110, which would have made a mid-sage post out of a near-black one. The brass goes the other way, lifted from a measured 108 to 124. An intermediate green at #2a4034 measured 58.5 -- dead centre of the window -- and produced holes at azimuth 0, which is how the arithmetic got checked. The departure from the measured green is real and is why this scores 0.88.

Four brass knobs instanced at the cornice corners -- one geometry, four placements, one draw call. At the corner posts' own +-0.153 m they sat inside the roof frustum and never rendered at all; the plate has them standing clear at the top rail's corners, so they are at +-0.175 m and outboard of the roof's slope.

assets.notes:
The decorative post used along Chao Phraya promenades, Rattanakosin footpaths and municipal park frontages -- much shorter than a road lighting column and read at pedestrian distance, so the moulded collar, flutes and lantern cap all have to be real geometry rather than texture. Sized from a 4 m mounting height; the plinth is about 0.4 m square and the lantern head about 0.35 m across. budgetClass is the derived large, which is right: the lantern head is the only expensive part and its six sides are one lathed or instanced form. Static: bolted to a plinth, so physics stays disabled.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED large -> hero (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.

WIDTH AND DEPTH CORRECTED 2026-08-31, 0.55 -> 0.42 m, from the plate and this entry's own notes agreeing against the declared figure. Masking the plate by hue (the prop is green cast iron, brass and glass against a NEUTRAL GREY GRADIENT backdrop, so a luma sweep test fails on it and a hue test does not) profiles the subject at 319 x 976 px: the plinth is the widest thing at 0.327 of the height, the column runs 0.121 and the lantern-and-roof 0.286. Those PROPORTIONS confirm the notes exactly -- lantern/plinth measures 0.874 against the notes' 0.35/0.40 = 0.875 -- while the plate's absolute scale does not, since at the declared 4.2 m height its plinth would be 1.37 m. So the notes' 0.40 m plinth is right and it is the widest part of the prop, which puts the envelope at 0.42 including the base step, not 0.55. Nothing on this post is 0.55 m across.

assets.name: Patchy Grass Ground Tile
assets.nameTh: พื้นหญ้าและดิน
assets.notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. There are no grass cards, no billboards and no alpha-tested blades: the grass is painted into the albedo with its clumping carried by the normal and AO maps, seen from standing eye height and above, which is the only way a ground cover fits this kit's budget. That is a deliberate limitation and it means the tile reads correctly from a walking camera and poorly from a camera lying on it. This is a member of the kit's ground-surface tile set: every tile in that set is 8 x 8 m, sits at y=0, uses pivot base-center and snaps on the kit's 8 m grid, so it butts flush against any other ground tile and against the asphalt road tiles, and the raised Concrete Sidewalk Strip (2.0 m wide, 0.15 m tall) sits alongside as a separate object. It is categorised as a building-part rather than as vegetation because it is a ground tile in that modular set and shares its whole contract; the vegetation category's size prior tops out around 3 m and describes potted plants and shrubs, which this is not. Coarse patchy grass worn through to red earth is the surface of Thai verges, temple and school grounds, park lawns, futsal-pitch surrounds and the strip between a soi and a wall -- always partly bare, because tropical lawn does not survive being walked on. Because the cover is irregular with no direction, it is fully FOUR-way rotationally symmetric and drops in at any of four orientations, which matters here because a large lawn is where a visible repeat shows worst. The first thing to check on the generated texture is that no distinctive bare patch or tuft appears twice across a seam. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. No destruction groups: a ground tile is static level geometry, not a breakable.

assets.name: Poured Concrete Apron Tile
assets.nameTh: พื้นคอนกรีต
assets.notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire surface reads out of the texture; the saw-cut joints are a normal and AO groove rather than modelled geometry. This is the plainest member of the kit's ground-surface tile set and the one that covers the most ground in a Thai scene after the interlocking paver: car parks, petrol station forecourts, factory and warehouse yards, temple aprons, rice-drying slabs and the surface of any soi that was concreted rather than surfaced. Every tile in the ground set is 8 x 8 m, sits at y=0, uses pivot base-center and snaps on the kit's 8 m grid, so it butts flush against any other ground tile and against the asphalt road tiles, and the raised Concrete Sidewalk Strip (2.0 m wide, 0.15 m tall) sits alongside as a separate object. The expansion joints form a SQUARE grid whose pitch must divide 8 m evenly and wrap on all four edges, which makes the tile fully FOUR-way rotationally symmetric -- it drops in at any of four orientations, and that plus the bay-to-bay tonal drift is what stops a large yard reading as a grid of identical copies. A broken joint line at a tile boundary is the first thing to check on the generated texture. Two things this tile is deliberately NOT: it carries no drain channels, no lid slabs and no edge bands, which is what separates it from the kit's older soi-alley-straight-tile, a 4 x 8 m alley piece with an open side drain painted into it; and it carries no road markings. One risk specific to this tile: flat pale grey concrete can land very close to the reference plate's grey backdrop and confuse a silhouette gate, so the generated plate needs real bay-to-bay tonal variation and staining rather than one even grey. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. No destruction groups: a ground tile is static level geometry, not a breakable. The rigid geometry on this tile is NOT generated: six seeds of the apron grid and one of the lane markings landed the pattern off the 8 m frame, breaking it at every boundary, so prompts.image asks the generator for the bare SURFACE only and scripts/tilekit/composite.mjs draws the geometry afterwards at known coordinates in metres. That is what makes the pitch divide 8 m and the lines wrap exactly, by construction rather than by luck, and it is the same split scripts/tilekit/substrates.mjs already uses for the road markings.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.86 -- not a pass self-score. The shape measures 0.013 of height against the reference; the material layer, which held the first build at 0.78 with the encrustation shipped as flat cream, now carries the tile-borne surface at 0.85. 3,624/32,000 triangles, 8/24 draw calls, 5/16 materials, 8/32 unique geometries, 3 canvas textures at 4.0 MB, factory ~75-140 ms.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 9.00 x 18.00 x 9.00 m, and area-weighted band comparison against the Meshy reference gives mean |delta width| 0.013 and |delta depth| 0.013 of height with every band inside 0.06 -- the closest proportional agreement of the whole batch.
featureReviews.notes: It was not close at first. Built to the plate's apparent proportions, band 2 came out 0.170 of height too wide -- the only band past the 0.12 flag anywhere in this batch. The plate is a three-quarter view from above and its foreshortening makes the platform look about a third of the prop's height; measured band by band, the reference puts the terrace top at 0.18 and shows nothing but tower across bands 2 to 5. The band table won and the terrace was rebuilt lower. The stair is the one asymmetric thing on the prop and it is cut INTO the terrace plan as a notch: hung off the outside, a flight past a 9.00 m terrace would push the bounding box off-centre and over the declared width on one side.

featureReviews.evidence: Eight receding redented tiers from 10.20 to 16.20 m, half-width 2.05 down to 0.50, each with a 0.10 m projecting ring band, closed by a lathed cap.
featureReviews.notes: The half-width follows a cosine raised to 1.5, which is what makes the taper CONVEX. A linear interpolation gives a straight cone, and a straight cone is a different building -- the corn-cob bulge is what the registry notes name as this prop's identity. Each lip starts 0.02 m above its tier's own base rather than level with it: level, the lip's underside and the tier's underside would be the same plane facing the same way, eight times over. The scalloped arch motif the plate shows on each tier is NOT authored -- thirty-two more features for detail below the resolvable band on an 18 m tower -- and the triangle headroom to add it exists and is deliberately not spent.

featureReviews.evidence: Blind arched door and raised arched pediment on each of four faces from ONE instanced unit, with eight red pilaster strips from a four-instance unit placed at radius zero.
featureReviews.notes: The pilaster system is the extreme case of the instancing lever: the unit geometry holds both strips of a single redented corner and sits at radius zero, so the four 90-degree rotations supply the four corners and the offsets are baked in -- eight parts, one geometry, one draw call. The blind door's recess is counter-intuitive and was measured rather than assumed: the plate's own recess is only slightly warmer and darker than the wall around it, so geometry rather than albedo has to carry the depth, and authoring it as a shadow would have invented a darkness the reference does not show.

featureReviews.evidence: Three notched slabs, a balustrade broken at the stair head, and a twelve-tread flight with raking cheeks -- twenty-two parts in ONE component and ONE draw call.
featureReviews.notes: Three separate z-fighting fixes here. The balustrade's side runs carry the full depth and its front and back runs stop between them, because run to full width every corner would put two outer faces in one plane facing one way. Each tread occupies only its own going rather than running back to the outer edge, so neighbours meet as opposed faces instead of twelve outer faces sharing a plane. And the slabs meet top-to-bottom, which is an opposed butt. check-coplanar reports the prop clean at 0.001 m.

The returns originally ran to the same depth as the front run and intersected it, smearing the canvas through the overlap; and `plain` was implemented as a sentinel slice index of -1, which still satisfied `i >= start && i < start+4` for vertices 0-2, so three corners of the +X face kept sampling the wordmark band. review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.86, up from 0.79, and the whole of the gain is that this prop finally HAS a proxy. Meshy still refuses the plate (content_policy_violation, safety checker forced on), but fal-ai/trellis and fal-ai/hunyuan3d/v2 both accept it, and two independent reconstructions agreeing is better evidence than one Meshy mesh. They put length/height at 1.852 and 2.020 against the build's 2.818 -- the hall was 46% too long -- and width/height at 1.226 and 1.265 against 1.410. Corrected to 12.38 x 10.00 x 19.24 m, the band table goes from mean |delta depth| 0.7267 to 0.0789 and |delta width| 0.1312 to 0.0739, with the bands over the 0.12 flag dropping from ten of ten to two. The roof was also the WRONG FORM: a gable, where the plate and both proxies show a hip. The remaining drag is materialSurface 0.82 and lightingCamera 0.80, and neither has an evidence-backed fix -- the plate is the darkest in the kit and its subject sits in its own shade, and a tile texture is exactly the opt-in the textureless default exists to refuse at prop distance. 2,892/32,000 triangles, 8/24 draw calls, 5/16 materials, 8/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: A 15.1 m figure on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade, head at +Z: one smooth body from neck to ankle, taller than deep, the upper leg a soft ridge on it, stacked feet with a toe comb, an upright tilted head with ushnisha and ear lobes cupped in the right hand, the forearm near-vertical from an elbow on the plinth, the left arm along the flank to a hand on the thigh.
featureReviews.notes: The only organic form in the kit, and it needed a shape helper written for it alone: a reclining body is a long soft mass whose section changes at every point along it, and a box decomposition of that is not a low-poly body but a pile of luggage. Every station's centre height is DERIVED from its own radius -- cy = plinth top + ry, computed rather than authored -- which is the only way a varying section can rest on a flat plinth at every point. The first promoted build was ONE symmetric tube from head to feet with the head at -Z, and it read as a figure on its back facing the wall; the rebuild carries the asymmetry that says on-its-side. Two earlier pose faults were found by review rather than by a gate: the arm ran too high and too far and covered the head entirely from the +X side, which is the only side anyone sees this prop from, and the ushnisha wanted 0.70 m of height where the soffit leaves 0.50. Reproportioned with the hall: it keeps the hall's own z scale and THICKENS -- 22.04 m of head-to-toe extent to 15.14 m and the section from 2.80 to 3.08 m, so length/depth goes 7.2 -> 4.9, which is what a human lying on its side actually measures and 7.2 is a pipe. The factor must be SZ and not something chosen to fill the hall: the figure does not sit in the hall, it sits on the PLINTH, which is scaled by SZ, and one build at 0.79 put the feet 1.1 m past the end of their own plinth and out through the end colonnade.

featureReviews.evidence: Twelve columns leaving the whole long front open, with the figure legible through them along its length and a dark interior face at luma 82 behind.
featureReviews.notes: The registry notes require this and give the reason: a closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all and reads as a warehouse. The interior shade fills the gaps between twelve columns, so its luma margin over the backdrop's 58 matters more here than anywhere -- at the backdrop value the gate would read eleven separate holes through the building. Its two panels also had to drop from 6.60 to 6.54: at the column head height each shared that plane with every column, and because the columns are an InstancedMesh, check-coplanar reported one mistake as twelve pairs.

featureReviews.evidence: Two HIPPED tiers at pitch 0.64 -- about 33 degrees -- sloping in on all four sides from eaves at 6.60 to a ridge at 9.68, each tier carrying an ochre eaves course under a red tile field, a capped rib down every one of its four hips and a capped ridge; the upper tier's eaves overhang the lower roof's surface by 0.25 m to make the double eave.
featureReviews.notes: This was a GABLE and it was the largest single error on the prop. Cropping the plate's roof out settles it in one look -- both tiers slope in at the ends, every corner wears a white-grey capped diagonal rib, and the ridge is a short capped line well inside the eaves -- and both proxies agree: the reference end elevation narrows steadily from eaves to ridge, which a gable cannot do. Built now through the preamble's hipRoof at curveExp 1, a straight Thai hip rather than a temple sweep, with ridgeHalfZ = hz - hx so the pitch is equal along both axes -- which is what a hip IS -- and y1 derived as y0 + pitch * hx so the pitch stays the one that was measured. Two cones per tier carry the banding: the gold cone is the whole tier, the red field starts one band up and stands 40 mm PROUD, because flush they would be coincident co-facing surfaces over the whole roof and inset the red would never be seen. The ribs are chained along hipRoof's own parametrisation, not aimed straight: the helper flares its eaves ring by 1 + 0.045 across the lower third whether or not cornerLift is zero, so the hip bows and a straight box cuts the chord and lifts off the surface at the eaves. The old bargeboard rake-angle bug -- atan(pitch) where atan2(run, rise) was wanted -- is gone with the bargeboards, which were rake boards for a form this prop does not have.

featureReviews.evidence: Five materials at PBR confidence 0.822-0.860, four measured on lit faces and the fifth corrected with its reasoning recorded.
featureReviews.notes: The gilt is the largest deliberate deviation on the prop. The figure is the ONE surface in this plate that is never directly lit -- deep shade, behind columns, under a soffit -- so its mean across 41,296 warm-hued pixels, #7D6040, is illumination and not albedo, and renders the figure brown. The albedo taken is the brightest QUARTILE of those pixels, #AC8E6F, which is the same 'measure a lit face' rule applied to a surface that has no lit face; the brightest 8% at #BEA07E was tried first and rendered cream. The plate cannot arbitrate this, and that is measured rather than assumed: a projective solve needs edges that are parallel in plan to be parallel in the image, and fitting the platform's ground silhouette gives four clean straight runs whose two must-be-parallel pairs differ in image slope by 47% and 34%. No single camera projects that -- the plate is a generated image and its perspective is only locally consistent. Do not re-attempt the solve here. The known proxy bias runs with the correction rather than against it: single-view reconstructions inflate depth, so if these two are wrong the true hall is shorter still, and 19.24 m is a floor.

Herringbone is deliberately the pattern rather than a running bond, because a herringbone is invariant under a 90 degree rotation: that makes this tile fully FOUR-way rotationally symmetric, so it drops in at any of four orientations and a large paved area does not read as a grid of identical copies. The pattern pitch must divide 8 m evenly and wrap on all four edges, or every tile boundary shows a broken diagonal -- that is the first thing to check on the generated texture, and a herringbone is unforgiving about it because the eye follows the diagonals straight across a seam. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. Quality comes entirely from a high-end tiling PBR texture set and not from mesh detail; that is the whole bet of this piece. assets.name: Road Straight Tile
assets.nameTh: ถนนตรง
assets.notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire street reads out of the texture: carriageway, lane markings, kerb line, sidewalk slabs, drain grates and manhole covers are painted into the maps, never built. The earlier procedural version of this tile modelled a raised 0.15 m kerb and sidewalk and it did not work, so the flat quad replaces it outright -- there is no kerb to step up onto and a player walks the sidewalk band at road level. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. Quality comes entirely from a high-end PBR texture generator -- albedo, roughness, normal and AO at photoreal fidelity matched to the reference plate -- and not from mesh detail; that is the whole bet of this piece. Fit is the one hard requirement: the footprint is exactly 8 x 8 m on the kit's 8 m grid, which is also the frontage of the kit's shop buildings so a tile row lines up with a shophouse row; the pivot is base-center so tiles snap on 8 m centres; and every road-facing edge carries the same band profile -- 1.25 m sidewalk, 5.5 m two-lane carriageway, 1.25 m sidewalk. Any tile edge must therefore meet any other, and the texture has to be edge-matched to the rest of the set at those band boundaries: asphalt tone, kerb-line position and sidewalk slab coursing must continue across a seam without a visible join. No destruction groups: a road tile is static level geometry, not a breakable. This is the plain repeating piece of the kit and will be instanced far more heavily than any other tile -- forty on screen at once is normal -- which is exactly why it is a single quad: forty of these is forty draw calls off one shared geometry and one shared material, and an InstancedMesh collapses it further. It carries no crossing, no junction and no branch; the storm drain is painted flush into the side band so nothing catches a player. Rotationally symmetric end to end, so it drops in at either of two orientations.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 3,698/4,000 triangles, 2/8 draw calls, 1/8 materials, 2/12 unique geometries, one 512 px canvas, factory built in 89 ms. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m; turntable PASSED with no --allow-holes. featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.366 x 0.182 x 0.958 m measured off the built module against a declared 0.35 x 0.20 x 0.95. Every trunk section comes from a column scan of the plate (scratch/_prop/dogscan.mjs): 0.998 mm/px along the long axis, which is the one axis the camera tilt does not foreshorten. Ribcage half-depth 0.121 x half-thickness 0.089 at z 0.010, loin tuck 0.104/0.080 at -0.085, hip 0.116/0.086 at -0.185, neck 0.058/0.050 at 0.255; the back edge follows the scan's own top line, which varies only 58 px over the whole trunk, so the spine is straight and the belly carries the change. Turntable ratios 0:1.000 90:1.218 180:0.939 270:1.259, gate PASSED with no --allow-holes.
featureReviews.notes: The DECLARED HEIGHT was corrected 0.28 -> 0.20 on the asset, with the arithmetic: 0.35 sin(phi) + h cos(phi) = 0.382 (the silhouette's image height over its length) has no solution at h = 0.28 for any plausible elevation, and solves at phi 42 for h = 0.20. Two residuals, both stated rather than averaged away: the plate's back-to-paw span implies a dog about 5% wider against its length than the declared box (inside the 0.10 tolerance), and the camera solve's two constraints land 13 degrees apart in elevation, which is the honest width of the section estimate at confidence 0.78. No proxy exists to close either.

featureReviews.evidence: The head is ONE 23-station sweep from the occiput to the nose with the STOP authored as a 12 mm station pair (section down 21%, dorsal line moving 13 mm toward the jaw) and a BLUNT muzzle end rather than a cone; a proud closed lid with a slit box on it; a nose pad. The up-side ear is two flaps -- a base rising off the crown at 17 degrees and a tip folded almost flat on it -- with its PLANE horizontal, which is where a dog's ear plane goes when the dog lies on its side, and is why the same ear is a rounded triangle in the plate's three-quarter and edge-on at azimuth 90. The down-side ear is splayed flat on the concrete with its base buried in the skull. Limbs leave the body as ellipsoid MASSES laid along their own segment, flatter in y than in x; below the elbow and hock they are tapering tubes with a joint ball at all four upper joints as well as the lower ones. Paws are flat ovals with two toe lobes on each forepaw and a dark pad cap on all four. The tail is three tapering pieces reaching 0.164 m past the rump with a light tip.
featureReviews.notes: Two attempts were made at the plate's 'ribs and hip bones visible under the coat' as an ilium and a scapula on the up-facing flank; a flattened ellipsoid intersecting a curved sweep shows its own flat top and both read as orange stickers at 7 mm proud and pale stickers at 1 mm. Removed, and the cue left to the fur canvas's cloudy drift, which is where it belongs at prop distance. The closed eye reads from above and barely from the side; the down-side ear is a coarse flap.

featureReviews.evidence: The coat is a [dorsal, ventral] colour PAIR per sweep station, blended around the ring: on an animal lying on its side the dorsal-to-ventral axis is HORIZONTAL, so an axis tint in x cuts the crown of the sweep in half and paints the up-facing flank as though it were the belly, and a multiply can only darken -- it can never take a warm tan to a cooler grey. The plate's own split is carried: saddle #be9871 (r - b = 77) against flank #908981 (r - b = 15), warm dorsally and neutral ventrally, coolest at the tuck that has been lying on the concrete. Along the body: pale collar, tan saddle, dusty flank, tan croup, pale tail tip. Limb masses carry the LOCAL crown tone. One 512 px fur canvas (7,200 directional strokes, cloudy drift, two soft bare patches) as map and bump.
featureReviews.notes: Every albedo is authored as the INVERSE of the harness transfer, which a probe of the first render's dorsal band gave as R = 0.62 A + 84 per channel; copying the plate straight in rendered the saddle as #cebfa2, a beige lump, which was the second build's whole coat failure. The transfer is orientation-dependent (0.985 A + 27 on a brighter face), so no single inverse is exact. Two tones DEPART from the plate and say so: the muzzle mask ships near luma 126 against a measured 50 and the nose at #3a302a against #2f2e2c, because both measurements sit under the harness backdrop's 58 where the turntable gate reads an enclosed surface as a HOLE -- the nose probed at luma 31 before the lift. assets.notes: subject is animal rather than prop, which selects the reconstruction profile with the chirality and swept-arc gates -- the landmark extractors are human-only, so animal does not run the anatomy track that character does. Left as prop it would be built with every one of those gates silently skipped, and a dog with two left forelegs would ship. Authored in one fixed sprawled sleeping pose and nothing else: the kit is static geometry with no rig and no animation, and a lying pose is the only one that reads correctly without either. No Meshy proxy exists (fal refuses the plate), so the plate is the only evidence and its image-vertical axis mixes the dorsoventral axis with height: v = -X sin(phi) + Y cos(phi). The whole-silhouette image height is 382 px of 952 across a 0.95 m length, and 0.35 sin(phi) + h cos(phi) = 0.382 has NO solution for h = 0.28 at any plausible camera elevation (0.35 x 0.28 needs phi above 75 or below 15 degrees, and the plate is a 40-45 degree three-quarter). At h = 0.20 it solves at phi = 42 degrees. The same solve gives a 0.230 m deep, 0.176 m thick ribcage. The second build reported a built 0.16 against the declaration and left the declaration standing; this corrects it. budgetClass re-pinned to large, which edit-assets reclassifies to medium on the resize.
